CHIEF RULING (recorded late -- it was posted to coordination at post-01M16YH9V69V0F8PYM1RB0Y030 in reply to m1's decision docket and never reached this bead).

YES: the resolved-but-unconcentrated mass goes into PlacementResolution's 'excluded' arm.

A unit resolved at 0.6 while a member of no class at 0.3 each is publishable by resolution and belongs to nothing being measured. Publishing a per-class metric for it is publishing a measurement we could not make -- Article I, in six metrics at once. It moves six published figures and that is acceptable under ADR 0003 provided the movement is ATTRIBUTABLE.

REQUIREMENT: record WHICH threshold each exclusion failed. Six metrics moving with an undifferentiated 'excluded' tells a later reader that something changed and not what.

I EXPLICITLY REJECTED the fallback m1 offered -- documenting that membership and resolution answer different questions -- not because it is wrong, but because a documented divergence between two 0.5 thresholds is a note somebody reads once, and an excluded arm is a property the type enforces forever.

Demonstrated rather than derived: 46f6b99 landed a fixture reaching Ambiguous, and the unit is publishable by resolution (0.6) while a member of no class (0.3 each). Two thresholds, both 0.5, different quantities.
